mainTopic: Which hair-made items can become impure through שרץ and מת, the גזירה שוה of 'בגד ועור', and the ornaments and atonement after the war with מדין.
overview: This amud opens with the last words of a גזירה שוה built on the word כלי. A ברייתא then teaches that a שק made of goat hair can become impure even if it is not woven. רבי יוחנן explains that such an item has a real use: a poor man braids three goat hairs into a necklace for his daughter. Another ברייתא reads 'או שק' to include reins and a saddle band, but not ropes and cords, because a sack is spun and woven. It then links the laws of שרץ and מת through a גזירה שוה on the words 'בגד ועור', after a simple logical comparison is rejected. Through that link, items made from horse-tail and cow-tail hair become impure in both kinds of טומאה. The גמרא shows that the words are מופנה (extra) on both sides, so the link cannot be refuted. The amud then turns to the war with מדין. It explains the ornaments עגיל and כומז and tells how the soldiers brought an offering to atone for sinful thoughts. A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל begins to explain why that generation needed atonement, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the earlier derivation from the word כלי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a derivation from the previous section. It learns one law from another through the shared word כלי (vessel).
steps.simpleTranslation: [We learn it from the word] 'vessel' here and 'vessel' there.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of a proof that started on the previous amud. The גמרא says the law is learned through a גזירה שוה on the word כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כלי appears in the laws of טומאת מת and also in the laws of other impurities. Because the same word appears in both places, the rule from one place is applied to the other. This line simply names the source and closes that discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessel or utensil. Here it is the shared word that links the two passages.
From there, meaning from the other passage.
A derivation that links two passages through an identical word.

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a discussion. Do not look for its question here. The question came at the end of the previous section.

phrases.english: 'Vessel', 'vessel' from there.
phrases.notes: This is shorthand for a גזירה שוה based on the repeated word כלי.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כְּלִי״ ״כְּלִי״ מֵהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began earlier.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The law is derived through a גזירה שוה on the word כלי.

steps.title: A sack is added to the category of garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It says a שק is added to the בגד category and is impure because of אריג (woven fabric).
steps.simpleTranslation: A sack is added to the garment, in that it is impure because of being woven fabric.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from a ברייתא as a base text so it can analyze it. The line says a שק joins the category of בגד for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about שרץ lists בגד, עור and שק. The ברייתא treats שק as an addition to בגד. It seems to give the reason as 'because it is woven.' The next step questions that wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Added. It is included as an extra item in a category.
Sackcloth, usually made of goat hair.
Garment or cloth.
Woven fabric.

phrases.english: A sack is added to the garment
in that it is impure because of being woven fabric.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּסָף שַׂק עַל הַבֶּגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion of a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שק is included in the category of בגד for טומאה.

steps.title: Isn't every garment already woven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the wording. Why say a שק is added 'because of אריג' when a בגד is itself woven?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that a garment is not woven fabric?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording. If a בגד is woven anyway, calling the שק 'added because it is woven' adds nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'added' should mean the שק brings something new to the category. But being woven is already true of every בגד. So the reason as written does not explain why the שק needed to be added.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? It opens a rhetorical challenge.
Not.

phrases.english: Is that to say that a garment is not woven fabric?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ בֶּגֶד לָאו אָרִיג הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'impure because of אריג' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בגד is already woven. So 'being woven' cannot be the new feature that justifies adding a שק.

steps.title: Rereading the line: a sack is impure even if not woven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. A שק is impure even though it is not woven, and that is the new point.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: a sack is added to the garment, in that even though it is not woven, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reinterpreting the ברייתא. The ברייתא was not saying the שק is impure because it is woven. It was saying the שק is impure even without being woven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'added' makes sense. A בגד must be woven to be impure, but goat-hair work is impure even when it is not woven. That is the real expansion the ברייתא teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. It introduces a reinterpretation.
Even though it is not.

steps.whatToRemember: The new point of the שק is that goat-hair items can be impure even without being woven.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
A sack is added to the garment,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ אָרִיג — טָמֵא.
phrases.english: in that even though it is not woven, it is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say the שק is impure because it is woven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the שק is impure even when it is not woven.

steps.title: What use is unwoven goat hair?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical use an unwoven goat-hair item has. Only a usable item can become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it fit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the new rule. It wants to know what an unwoven goat-hair item could actually be used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object needs a real use to count as a כלי that can become impure. Unwoven goat hair sounds useless. So the גמרא asks how it could be important enough to receive טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: For what is it fit? What is it useful for?

phrases.english: For what is it fit?
phrases.notes: It asks about an unwoven goat-hair item.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the practical side of the answer in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic use for unwoven goat hair that would make it a functional item.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a poor man's braided ornament
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that a poor person braids three goat hairs and hangs them on his daughter's neck as jewelry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because a poor person braids three hairs and hangs it on his daughter's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a real-life use for unwoven goat hair. Even a few braided hairs can serve as a necklace for a poor girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Braiding is not weaving, yet the result is a usable object. That gives unwoven goat hair the status of a functional item, which can become impure. This supports the reading from step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person.
Braids.
Hairs or strands.
Neck.

steps.whatToRemember: Even three braided goat hairs used as a necklace count as a usable item, so they can be impure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because a poor person braids three hairs
and hangs it on his daughter's neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁכֵּן עָנִי קוֹלֵעַ שָׁלֹשׁ נִימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Braided goat hair serves as a poor girl's necklace, so it is a usable item.

steps.title: 'Or sack' includes reins and a saddle band
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא learns from the words 'או שק' that reins (קילקלי) and a saddle band (חבק) are also included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Sack' teaches me only a sack. From where do we include the reins and the saddle band? The verse says: 'Or sack.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that reads the verse closely. The extra word 'או' (or) widens the category beyond an actual sack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שק alone would cover only a real sack. The added word 'או' teaches that similar goat-hair items are included too. These items, reins and a saddle band, are not containers or garments.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. It introduces a ברייתא.
From where do we include?
Reins or a harness strap for an animal.
A girth band fastened under an animal's belly.
The verse teaches.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Sack': I have only a sack,

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַקִּילְקְלִי וְאֶת הַחֲבָק —
phrases.english: from where do we include the reins and the saddle band?
The verse says: 'Or sack.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״שָׂק״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שַׂק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא on the same verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'או' includes reins and a saddle band in the category of שק.

steps.title: Should ropes and cords be included too?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible overreach. Perhaps 'או' also includes ropes and measuring cords.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think that I include the ropes and the cords.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possibility it will reject in the next step. Since 'או' widened the category, maybe it widens it to all ropes and cords.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a word widens a category, we must ask where the widening stops. Ropes and cords are also used with animals and goods. So without a limit, they might seem to belong.

keyTerms.meaning: I might think. It introduces a mistaken assumption.
Ropes.
Cords, such as measuring cords.

phrases.english: I might think that I include
the ropes and the cords.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the inclusion from step 7 reaches.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'או' widens the category, nothing yet stops it from including every rope and cord.

steps.title: Only spun and woven items, like a sack
steps.stepSummary: The word שק sets the limit. Only items that are spun and woven like a sack are included, so ropes and cords are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Sack.' Just as a sack is spun and woven, so too anything spun and woven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the overreach of step 8. It uses the word שק itself as the model for what counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'או' widens the category, but the word שק keeps it close to its model. A sack is made of spun thread that is then woven, so only items made that way are included. Ropes and cords are not made that way, so they stay out.

keyTerms.meaning: Spun into thread.
Just as ... so too. It introduces a comparison that sets a limit.

steps.whatToRemember: 'או שק' includes items made like a sack, such as reins and a saddle band. It excludes ropes and cords, which are not spun and woven.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'Sack.'
Just as a sack is spun and woven,
so too anything spun and woven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״שָׂק״. מָה שַׂק טְוִוי וְאָרִיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possibility raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the inclusion by comparing to the model item (the sack).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'או' might include every rope and cord.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only items that are spun and woven like a sack are included.

steps.title: The verse about מת includes reins and the band too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points to the verse about טומאת מת. Its phrase 'all work of goats' includes reins and a saddle band in the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, it says regarding a corpse: 'And every vessel of leather and all work of goats' hair... you shall purify.' This comes to include the reins and the saddle band.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא cites a parallel verse from the laws of מת. That verse also brings reins and a saddle band into the category of goat-hair items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'כל מעשה עזים' is broad, so it covers goat-hair items that are not sacks, like reins and a saddle band. The laws of מת therefore reach the same result as 'או שק' in the laws of שרץ. The two sources agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, it says. It introduces a supporting verse.
A corpse, the source of טומאת מת.
Work made of goats' hair.
You shall purify.

steps.whyThisMatters: Both kinds of impurity end up with the same list of included goat-hair items. That keeps the laws of טומאה consistent.

phrases.english: Now, it says regarding a corpse:
'And every vessel of leather
and all work of goats' hair, etc., you shall purify'
to include the reins and the saddle band.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר בְּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the parallel inclusion for מת from 'כל מעשה עזים'. Step 11 then tests how far this inclusion reaches.
steps.raayaObject: Reins and a saddle band are included among goat-hair items that can become impure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For טומאת מת, the phrase 'כל מעשה עזים' includes reins and a saddle band.

steps.title: Maybe the verse about מת includes ropes and cords
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the broad phrase 'all work of goats' in the verse about מת also includes ropes and cords.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might have thought that I would include even the ropes and the thin cords.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 10 the verse about מת included reins and a saddle band through the phrase 'all work of goats'. Now the ברייתא worries that this broad phrase might include too much, even ropes and cords.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שרץ, the word שק already limited the rule to spun-and-woven items (step 9). The verse about מת has no word שק, so nothing seems to stop its broad wording. The ברייתא now has to find a limit for מת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I might have thought'. It opens a possible but mistaken reading.
Ropes
Thin cords, such as measuring cords
A corpse. It gives the most severe form of טומאה.

phrases.english: I might have thought that I include
even the ropes and the thin cords?
phrases.notes: This is said about טומאת מת, which the verse calls 'all work of goats'.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אֶת הַחֲבָלִים וְאֶת הַמְּשִׁיחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges how far the inclusion from step 10 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The broad phrase 'all work of goats' in the verse about מת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse about מת has no limiting word like שק. So its broad wording might seem to include ropes and cords.

steps.title: A logical comparison: מת should follow שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a simple logical comparison. Both שרץ and מת make things טמא, so מת should also apply only to spun-and-woven items.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is logical: the Torah made things impure through a שרץ, and it made things impure through a מת. Just as with שרץ it only made spun-and-woven items impure, so too with מת it only makes spun-and-woven items impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to answer step 11 with plain logic, without a verse. It compares מת to שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that these are two parallel kinds of טומאה, so they should have the same limits. With שרץ we already know only טווי ואריג counts, so the same should be true for מת. This answer will be tested in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is logical'. A proof from reasoning, not from a verse.
A dead creeping creature. It gives a lighter form of טומאה.
Spun and woven
It made something ritually impure

phrases.english: And it is logical:
the Torah made things impure through a creeping creature, and made things impure through a corpse.
Just as, when it made things impure through a creeping creature,
it only made spun and woven items impure,
so too, when it makes things impure through a corpse,
it only makes spun and woven items impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא: טִימֵּא בַּשֶּׁרֶץ, וְטִימֵּא בַּמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question of step 11 using logic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical comparison (דין) between two kinds of טומאה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מת might include ropes and cords because of its broad wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: מת, like שרץ, applies only to spun-and-woven items.

steps.title: The comparison fails: מת is more severe
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the logical comparison. Being lenient with the lighter טומאה of שרץ does not prove we should be lenient with the stricter טומאה of מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wait: if the Torah was lenient with the טומאה of שרץ, which is light, should we be lenient with the טומאה of מת, which is severe?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down its own logical answer from step 12. The two kinds of טומאה are not equal, so one cannot be compared to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of מת is more severe than the טומאה of שרץ. So it could easily reach more items, even ropes. A leniency found in the lighter case cannot be carried over to the stricter case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Behold' or 'but wait'. It opens a point that separates two cases.
Light, less severe
Severe, stricter
Shall we be lenient?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the הלכה itself. The ברייתא is only rejecting the logical method from step 12. The conclusion stays the same, but it will now be proven from a verse instead.

phrases.english: But wait: if the Torah was lenient with the impurity of a creeping creature,
which is light,
shall we be lenient with the impurity of a corpse,
which is severe?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵן אִם הֵיקֵל בְּטוּמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ שֶׁהִיא קַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the logical comparison of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the logical comparison (דין), not the final ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It compares a light טומאה to a severe one. A leniency in the lighter case does not carry over to the stricter case.

steps.title: The verse gives a גזירה שוה using 'בגד ועור'
steps.stepSummary: Since logic failed, the ברייתא brings a verse. The matching words 'בגד ועור' appear with both שרץ and מת, and they create a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says 'garment and leather' and 'garment and leather', to create a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא replaces the failed logic with a Torah-based link. This step announces the tool, and the next step shows how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is a link the Torah makes through matching words. Because it comes from the Torah, the difference in severity between the two cases does not matter. That is why it succeeds where the logical comparison failed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches'. It introduces proof from a verse.
A link between two laws based on the same words appearing in both
A garment and leather

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle. When logic can be pushed back by a difference between the cases, the ברייתא turns to a verse-based גזירה שוה. Later the גמרא explains that such a link is protected from refutation only when its words are מופנה (extra).

phrases.english: Therefore the verse teaches
'garment and leather', 'garment and leather',
to create a verbal analogy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״בֶּגֶד״ וָ״עוֹר״ ״בֶּגֶד״ וָ״עוֹר״ לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It replaces the logic rejected in step 13 with a Torah-based link.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a verse, the stricter טומאה of מת might include ropes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Matching words connect מת to שרץ.

steps.title: From שרץ to מת: only spun and woven items
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא spells out the גזירה שוה. Just as 'בגד ועור' with שרץ covers only spun-and-woven items, so does 'בגד ועור' with מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Garment and leather' is said about שרץ, and 'garment and leather' is said about מת. Just as with שרץ only spun-and-woven items become impure, so too with מת only spun-and-woven items become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows how the גזירה שוה works in the first direction, from שרץ to מת. This finally answers step 11: ropes and cords are not included with מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit that שרץ has from the word שק now passes over to מת through the shared words. So ropes and cords are excluded from מת as well, even though מת is more severe.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is said', meaning stated in the verse
Which is said, the one mentioned

phrases.english: 'Garment and leather' is said about a creeping creature,
and 'garment and leather' is said about a corpse.
Just as the garment and leather mentioned with a creeping creature
only made spun and woven items impure,
so too the garment and leather mentioned with a corpse
only makes spun and woven items impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר ״בֶּגֶד״ וָ״עוֹר״ בְּשֶׁרֶץ וְנֶאֱמַר ״בֶּגֶד״ וָ״עוֹר״ בְּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It applies the גזירה שוה announced in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: מת includes only spun-and-woven items, so ropes and cords are excluded
steps.raayaSupportSource: The גזירה שוה of 'בגד ועור' in the verses about שרץ and מת

steps.title: From מת to שרץ: all goat-hair work
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה works in the other direction too. Just as with מת all goat-hair work becomes impure, so too with שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as 'garment and leather' said about מת makes all goat-hair work impure, so too 'garment and leather' said about שרץ makes all goat-hair work impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא runs the same link backward, from מת to שרץ. This closes the section: both kinds of טומאה now share the same rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מת, the phrase 'all work of goats' includes items like reins and a saddle band (step 10). Through the shared words, that inclusion now carries over to שרץ too. So the two laws match fully: only spun-and-woven items, plus all goat-hair work.

keyTerms.meaning: All work made of goat hair
'And just as'. It opens the comparison in the reverse direction.

steps.whatToRemember: The גזירה שוה of 'בגד ועור' teaches in both directions. From שרץ, מת learns that only spun-and-woven items count, so ropes and cords are out. From מת, שרץ learns that all goat-hair work counts, like reins and a saddle band.

phrases.english: And just as the garment and leather mentioned with a corpse
made all goat-hair work impure,
so too the garment and leather mentioned with a creeping creature
makes all goat-hair work impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה בֶּגֶד וָעוֹר הָאָמוּר בְּמֵת טִמֵּא כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה עִזִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It runs the same גזירה שוה in the reverse direction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rules of שרץ and מת are fully linked. Both include only spun-and-woven items, and both include all goat-hair work.

steps.title: What about items made from horse-tail or cow-tail hair?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that so far we only learned about goat products, and asks for a source for items made from horse-tail and cow-tail hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about something that comes from goats. From where do we include something that comes from a horse's tail or a cow's tail?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a new question. The גזירה שוה only covered goat products, so it wants a source for items made from horse-tail or cow-tail hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כל מעשה עזים' (all work of goats) only mention goats. So the source we have so far covers goat products and nothing else. The ברייתא now wants to stretch the rule to hair from other animals' tails.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only have…' — the source so far covers only this case
From where do we include (add on) more cases?
Goats
A horse's tail (its hair is used for weaving)

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא דָּבָר הַבָּא מִן הָעִזִּים,
phrases.english: I only have [a source for] something that comes from goats;
from where do we include something that comes
from a horse's tail or from a cow's tail?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא דָּבָר הַבָּא מִן הָעִזִּים, מִנַּיִין לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the גזירה שוה from Steps 15–16. It points out that the source only mentions goats and asks how to go further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source from the תורה that items made from horse-tail or cow-tail hair can become טמא.

steps.title: The words 'or a sack' include them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the words 'או שק' in the verse about שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'or a sack.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a verse. The words 'או שק' (or a sack) in the passage about שרץ include items made from horse-tail and cow-tail hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sack is woven from coarse hair. So 'או שק' teaches that other hair-woven things, like horse-tail and cow-tail work, can also become טמא. This adds animals beyond goats.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches' — introduces the source
A sack, usually woven from coarse hair

phrases.english: The verse says: 'or a sack.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא י״א:ל״ב, in the passage about שרץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אוֹ שָׂק״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'או שק' include items made from horse-tail and cow-tail hair.

steps.title: But those words were already used for reins and a saddle band
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'או שק' was already used to include קילקלי and חבק, so it cannot teach a second thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you already use [these words] for reins and a saddle band?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The words 'או שק' were already used up to teach about reins and a saddle band.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one extra phrase in the verse teaches only one thing. Since 'או שק' was already used for קילקלי וחבק, how can it also teach about horse-tail and cow-tail hair? It looks like the ברייתא is using the same words twice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But you already took it out (used it) for…'
Reins or straps used on an animal
A saddle band (girth strap)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying reins and saddle bands are pure. It is only asking whether the words 'או שק' are free to teach a second law.

phrases.english: But didn't you already use it for reins and a saddle band?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַפֵּיקְתֵּיהּ לְקִילְקְלִי וַחֲבָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'או שק' as the source for horse-tail and cow-tail items.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One phrase cannot teach two laws, and 'או שק' was already used for קילקלי וחבק.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה frees the words for a new teaching
steps.stepSummary: Before the גזירה שוה, 'או שק' was needed for reins and a saddle band. Now the גזירה שוה covers them, so 'או שק' is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was only before the גזירה שוה came. Now that the גזירה שוה has come, [the words] are extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Once the גזירה שוה brings in 'all goat-hair work', reins and a saddle band are already covered, so 'או שק' is free to teach about horse-tail and cow-tail hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reins and saddle bands count as goat-hair work. Step 16 showed that the גזירה שוה applies all goat-hair work to שרץ too. So 'או שק' is no longer needed for them and can teach a new law.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These words apply…' — limits the earlier point to a certain stage
Before it came
Now that it has come
It became extra, free for a new teaching

steps.whatToRemember: An extra word in a verse is used to teach something new. When another source already covers its old job, the word is freed up for a new law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one derivation changes another. The גזירה שוה takes over one job, so the verse's words become free for another.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי מִקַּמֵּי דְּתֵיתֵי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה,
phrases.english: That was only before the verbal analogy came;
now that the verbal analogy has come,
it [the phrase 'או שק'] is extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי מִקַּמֵּי דְּתֵיתֵי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 using the גזירה שוה of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Freed-up phrase: another source takes over the old job, so the extra words can teach something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'או שק' is used up on reins and a saddle band.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה covers reins and a saddle band as goat-hair work. So 'או שק' teaches about horse-tail and cow-tail items.

steps.title: Does the horse-tail rule also apply to טומאת מת?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that 'או שק' is written about שרץ, and asks for a source for טומאת מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only have this for שרץ. From where do we know it for טומאת מת?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up its next move. The words 'או שק' appear only in the passage about שרץ, so it asks how we know horse-tail items also become טמא through a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new teaching came from a verse about שרץ. So for now it covers only שרץ. The ברייתא now looks for a way to carry it over to מת. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping creature whose dead body makes things טמא
The impurity caused by a human corpse

phrases.english: And I only have [this] with a creeping creature;
with impurity from a corpse, from where [do we know it]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּשֶׁרֶץ, בְּטוּמְאַת מֵת מִנַּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that horse-tail items are settled for שרץ, it asks whether the rule also applies to מת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that items made from horse-tail or cow-tail hair become טמא through טומאת מת, not only through שרץ.

steps.title: A logical comparison between corpse and creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tries to answer the question about מת with a logical argument. The Torah gave impurity to both מת and שרץ. Just as with שרץ, horse-tail and cow-tail items count like goat-hair items, so too with מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it makes logical sense. The Torah made things impure through a corpse, and it made things impure through a שרץ. With שרץ, the Torah treated things made from horse tail and cow tail just like things made from goat hair. So with a corpse too, it should treat things made from horse tail and cow tail just like things made from goat hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its first attempt to answer the question from step 21. It uses plain logic, a comparison, instead of a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both שרץ and מת are sources of impurity that make garments and similar items impure. Since the law for שרץ is already known (from 'או שק'), the ברייתא wants to copy that law over to מת. The argument rests only on the idea that the two cases are similar enough.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is logical.' This opens a reasoning-based proof, not a proof from a verse.
A corpse, the source of טומאת מת
One of the eight creeping animals whose dead body makes things impure
Horse tail and cow tail. Their hair is woven into items.
Things made from goat products, such as goat hair

phrases.english: And it is logical:
He rendered impure with a corpse, and He rendered impure with a creeping animal.
phrases.notes: 'He' means the Torah.

phrases.english: Just as when He rendered impure with a creeping animal,
He made a thing that comes
from a horse's tail and from a cow's tail
like something made from goats,
so too when He rendered impure with a corpse,
He made a thing that comes
from a horse's tail and from a cow's tail
like something made from goats.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first, logic-based answer to the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Compare מת to שרץ by logic. Since horse-tail and cow-tail items count like goat items for שרץ, they should count that way for מת too.

steps.title: The comparison fails: wide evening impurity versus limited seven-day impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the logical comparison. שרץ impurity lasts only until evening and covers many cases. מת impurity lasts seven days and covers fewer cases. Something added to the wide category cannot simply be added to the narrow, strict one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really? If the Torah added more items to the impurity that lasts until evening, which is a wide category, should we add them to the impurity that lasts seven days, which is a small, limited category?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back against its own logical proof from step 22 and shows why it does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impurity that lasts until evening (like שרץ) is common, and the Torah applies it widely. The seven-day impurity of מת is rare and more limited. So the fact that the Torah widened the common category does not prove it widened the limited one. The logic of step 22 is therefore too weak.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Indeed?' A word that opens a rejection: are these really comparable?
He included or added more items
Impurity that lasts until nightfall, like that of a שרץ
Impurity that lasts seven days, like that of a מת
Widespread (applies in many cases) / limited (applies in fewer cases)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get confused here. טומאת מת is the more severe impurity. 'מוּעֶטֶת' does not mean it is weaker. It means it applies in fewer cases. That is exactly why we should not easily widen it.

phrases.english: Indeed, if He added
to the impurity lasting until evening, which is widespread,
shall we add to the seven-day impurity
which is limited?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵן אִם רִיבָּה בְּטוּמְאַת עֶרֶב שֶׁהִיא מְרוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical comparison made in step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole logical comparison between שרץ and מת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two kinds of impurity are not equal. שרץ impurity is common and wide. מת impurity is rare and limited, so adding to the first does not prove adding to the second.

steps.title: The source is a גזירה שוה from 'garment' and 'leather'
steps.stepSummary: Since logic failed, the ברייתא brings a verse-based link. The words 'בגד' and 'עור' appear both in the שרץ passage and in the מת passage. That shared wording teaches that the horse-tail and cow-tail rule of שרץ also applies to מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'garment' and 'leather', 'garment' and 'leather', for a גזירה שוה. 'Garment' and 'leather' are said about a שרץ, and 'garment' and 'leather' are said about a corpse. Just as with the 'garment and leather' said about a שרץ, the Torah treated horse-tail and cow-tail items like goat items, so too with the 'garment and leather' said about a corpse, the Torah treated horse-tail and cow-tail items like goat items.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its real answer to the question from step 21. It uses a גזירה שוה, a link between two passages that share the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה links two passages through shared words, not through a comparison of how alike the cases are. Because the same words 'בגד' and 'עור' appear in both places, the law known for שרץ carries over to מת. The next step adds a condition: the link is safe from a logical refutation only if the words are מופנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches.' This brings a proof from the Torah's wording.
A link between two passages based on a shared word or phrase. The law of one passage is applied to the other.
A garment
Leather
Which is stated (in a certain passage)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final source for the ברייתא. Items woven from horse-tail and cow-tail hair become impure from a corpse, just as they do from a שרץ.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'Garment' and 'leather', 'garment' and 'leather', for a verbal analogy.
'Garment' and 'leather' is said about a creeping animal,
phrases.notes: ויקרא יא:לב

phrases.english: and 'garment' and 'leather' is said about a corpse.
phrases.notes: במדבר לא:כ

phrases.english: Just as with the 'garment and leather' stated about a creeping animal,
He made a thing that comes
from a horse's tail and from a cow's tail
like something made from goats,
so too with the 'garment and leather' stated about a corpse,
He made a thing that comes
from a horse's tail and from a cow's tail
like something made from goats.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: בֶּגֶד וָעוֹר בֶּגֶד וָעוֹר לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected logical proof of step 22 with a verse-based גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the words 'בגד' and 'עור', which appear in both the שרץ passage and the מת passage.

steps.title: The analogy must be built on extra words, or it could be broken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a condition. The words used for this גזירה שוה must be 'מופנה', meaning extra and not needed for anything else. Otherwise someone could break the link, because a שרץ is stricter: it makes things impure at the size of a lentil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the words must be free. Because if they were not free, one could break the comparison: what is special about a שרץ? It makes things impure with just a lentil-sized piece!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains a requirement for the גזירה שוה of step 24 to work. The words must be extra, so that no one can argue against the link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal גזירה שוה can be challenged if one side has a special strictness. Here, a שרץ makes things impure even at the size of a lentil (כעדשה), while a corpse needs an olive's size (כזית). So someone could say the שרץ law is unique. But if the words are 'מופנה', extra and placed in the Torah only for this link, such a challenge does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Free or extra. These words are not needed for their own passage, so they are available for a גזירה שוה.
'One could refute.' A difference between the two cases could break the comparison.
'Since it' or 'for it.' This introduces the special feature of one side.
The size of a lentil, the minimum amount of a שרץ that makes things impure

steps.whatToRemember: Horse-tail and cow-tail items become impure through טומאת מת by a גזירה שוה from 'בגד' and 'עור'. This works only because the words are מופנה. Without that, the extra strictness of שרץ (impurity at כעדשה) could break the link.

phrases.english: And it is free.
phrases.notes: The words used for the גזירה שוה must be extra.

phrases.english: For if it were not free,
one could refute it:
What about a creeping animal,
since it makes things impure with a lentil-sized piece?!
phrases.notes: A corpse makes things impure only with an olive-sized piece.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוּפְנֶה. דְּאִי לָאו מוּפְנֶה אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a condition for the גזירה שוה of step 24: the words must be extra, so the analogy cannot be broken.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה of 'בגד ועור' must be built on extra words (מופנה). Otherwise the stricter nature of שרץ, which makes things impure at the size of a lentil, would break the analogy.

steps.title: The words בגד and עור are extra in the שרץ passage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that בגד and עור in the שרץ passage are extra. A היקש already links שרץ to שכבת זרע, and the שכבת זרע passage already mentions בגד and עור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, they are free. שרץ is placed right next to שכבת זרע in the Torah. The שכבת זרע passage already says 'every garment and every hide'. So why does the Torah need to write 'garment' and 'hide' again by שרץ? This shows they were written to be free for the גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the condition from the last step by showing that בגד and עור in the שרץ passage really are extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah puts שרץ right next to שכבת זרע, and this closeness makes a היקש that lets us apply the rules of one to the other. Since the שכבת זרע passage already says בגד and עור, we would know the same rule for שרץ without being told. So the Torah's words בגד and עור by שרץ are not needed for their own rule, and they are free to be used for the גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, truly (an affirming word)
Is compared through a היקש, meaning the Torah placed the two topics side by side so they share rules
Semen, which carries a form of טומאה
And right next to it (in the verses)
Why do I need it? This signals that a word looks extra
To make it free (מופנה) for a גזירה שוה

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not that שרץ never needs a rule about garments. The point is that the rule could already be learned through the היקש from שכבת זרע, so the Torah's own words by שרץ are left over.

phrases.english: Indeed, they are free (extra).
Now, since a creeping animal is juxtaposed to semen,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָרַע״,
phrases.english: as it is written: 'a man from whom semen is emitted',
phrases.notes: ויקרא כב:ד

phrases.aramaic: וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ: ״אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל שֶׁרֶץ״,
phrases.english: and right next to it: 'a man who touches any creeping animal',
phrases.notes: ויקרא כב:ה

phrases.english: and it is written regarding semen:
'and every garment and every hide
on which there is semen' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא טו:יז

phrases.english: so 'garment' and 'hide' that the Torah wrote about a creeping animal,
why do I need them?
Learn from this that they are there to be free.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאיֵי אִפְּנוֹיֵי מוּפְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the condition set in step 25 (the words must be מופנה) is fulfilled, at least on the שרץ side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the words בגד and עור really extra, so the גזירה שוה cannot be refuted?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. In the שרץ passage they are extra, because the היקש to שכבת זרע would already teach the same rule.

steps.title: The link is free on only one side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that only the שרץ side has been shown to be extra. A link that is מופנה on one side satisfies the opinion of למדין ואין משיבין, but not the opinion of למדין ומשיבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, it is free on only one side. That works for the one who says that a link free on one side can be used to learn, and cannot be refuted. But for the one who says you can learn from it and also refute it, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. It points out that the words were shown to be extra only in the שרץ passage, not in the מת passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known dispute about a גזירה שוה that is free on only one side. One opinion says we learn from it and no one may refute it with a logical difference. The other opinion says we learn from it, but it can still be refuted. Under that second opinion, the difference raised in step 25 (שרץ makes things impure at the size of a lentil) would break the link again.

keyTerms.meaning: But still
Free on only one side, meaning the word is extra in only one of the two passages
We learn from it, and it cannot be refuted
We learn from it, but it can be refuted by a logical difference
It works out well according to the one who says
What can be said? It presses for an answer, which the next step gives.

phrases.english: But still, it is free on only one side.
This works well according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: מוּפְנֶה מִצַּד אֶחָד לְמֵידִין וְאֵין מְשִׁיבִין.
phrases.english: that from a link free on one side we learn, and do not refute.
But according to the one who says we learn and also refute,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי מוּפְנֶה מִצַּד אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the step 26 proof but argues that it is not enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 26 that the גזירה שוה is safe from refutation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the שרץ side was shown to be extra. Under the opinion of למדין ומשיבין, a link free on one side can still be broken by the difference that שרץ makes things impure at the size of a lentil.

steps.title: The words are also extra in the מת passage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בגד and עור are extra in the מת passage too. A היקש also links מת to שכבת זרע, so the גזירה שוה is free on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words written about מת are also free. מת is placed right next to שכבת זרע: 'whoever touches anything impure by the dead, or a man from whom semen is emitted'. The שכבת זרע passage already says 'every garment and every hide'. So why does the Torah write 'garment' and 'hide' about מת? This shows they were written to be free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by using the same kind of proof on the מת side. This shows the words are extra there as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same verse (ויקרא כב:ד) puts טמא נפש, meaning someone impure from a dead body, right next to שכבת זרע. That makes a היקש, so the mention of בגד and עור by שכבת זרע would already cover מת. This means the words by מת are also extra, the link is free on both sides, and everyone agrees it cannot be refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone or something impure from a dead body
Also
Free on both sides (the idea behind this answer, though not the words in the text). A link like this cannot be refuted according to everyone.

steps.whatToRemember: The גזירה שוה of בגד and עור between שרץ and מת is free on both sides. Each side is extra because of a היקש to שכבת זרע. So the horse-tail and cow-tail rule of שרץ also applies to מת, and according to every opinion it cannot be refuted.

phrases.english: The words regarding a corpse are also free:
Now, since a corpse is juxtaposed to semen,
as it is written: 'and whoever touches anything impure by the dead

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָרַע״,
phrases.english: or a man from whom semen is emitted',
phrases.notes: ויקרא כב:ד

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב בְּשִׁכְבַת זֶרַע: ״וְכׇל בֶּגֶד וְכׇל עוֹר״ —
phrases.english: and it is written regarding semen: 'and every garment and every hide' —
so 'garment' and 'hide' that the Torah wrote about a corpse,
why do I need them?
Learn from this that they are there to be free.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמֵת נָמֵי אִפְּנוֹיֵי מוּפְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27 by showing the second side is free too.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends the same proof to the other side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought only the שרץ side was extra, so the link could be refuted under the opinion of למדין ומשיבין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מת side is also extra because of its היקש to שכבת זרע. The link is free on both sides and cannot be refuted.

steps.title: The verse about the gold ornaments from the war with מדין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes topic. It quotes the verse listing the gold ornaments the soldiers brought as an offering after the war with מדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And we have brought the offering of ה׳, what each man found of gold items: anklets and bracelets, a ring, an עגיל, and a כומז.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of טומאה and goes back to the verses about the war with מדין. It quotes this verse to set up an explanation of two of its words in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a setup step. The list of jewelry belongs to the larger discussion of ornaments, and the last two words, עגיל and כומז, are unclear. The next step explains them.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering to ה׳
An ornament worn on the arm or leg, such as an anklet or armlet
A bracelet
A ring

phrases.english: 'And we have brought the offering of the Lord,
what each man found of gold items:
anklets and bracelets, a ring, an agil, and a kumaz.'
phrases.notes: במדבר לא:נ

steps.triggerLanguage: וַנַּקְרֵב אֶת קׇרְבַּן ה׳ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָצָא כְלִי זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the טומאה discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the verse whose unclear words will be explained next.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains עגיל and כומז
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the two unclear words. An עגיל is an ornament shaped like a woman's breasts, and a כומז is an ornament shaped like the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: An עגיל is a mold in the shape of the breasts. A כומז is a mold in the shape of the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains what the two strange jewelry words in the verse mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both items were molded ornaments that women wore over those parts of the body. This sets up the discussion below of the offering the soldiers brought, which the גמרא explains was atonement for improper thoughts.

keyTerms.meaning: An ornament molded in the shape of the breasts
An ornament molded in the shape of the womb
A mold or molded shape
The womb

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
An agil is a mold in the shape of the breasts.
A kumaz is a mold in the shape of the womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words in the verse quoted in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עגיל is a breast-shaped ornament, and a כומז is a womb-shaped ornament.

steps.title: רב יוסף supports the reading from the Aramaic translation
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that if רבי אלעזר is right about כומז, this explains why the תרגום translates it as מָחוֹךְ, something that leads to foolishness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If so, that is why we translate it as 'מחוך', an item that leads to foolishness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings support for רבי אלעזר's explanation that a כומז was an ornament shaped like the womb. He points to how the Aramaic translation renders the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרגום translates כומז as מחוך, which sounds like גיחוך, meaning silly or lewd behavior. That fits an ornament with an immodest shape. So the translation matches רבי אלעזר's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is correct
We translate it, referring to the Aramaic תרגום
The תרגום's Aramaic word for כומז
Foolishness or frivolous behavior

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: If so,
that is why we translate it as 'machokh'
phrases.notes: This refers to the Aramaic translation of כומז.

phrases.english: an item that leads to foolishness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's definition of כומז from Step 30.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's claim that a כומז was an ornament shaped like the womb
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Aramaic תרגום, which renders כומז as מחוך, something that leads to גיחוך

steps.title: רבה says the word itself already shows the meaning
steps.stepSummary: רבה says there is no need for the תרגום, because the word כומז itself hints at the meaning: כאן מקום זימה, 'here is the place of lewdness'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: You can learn this from the verse itself. 'כומז' stands for 'כאן מקום זימה', here is the place of lewdness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה tells רב יוסף that the proof can come straight from the word in the verse, without the translation. He reads כומז as short for three words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה reads כומז as an abbreviation: כ for כאן, מ for מקום, and ז for זימה. This shows the ornament was tied to an immodest place. רבה agrees with the meaning and only offers a more direct source.

keyTerms.meaning: From the verse itself
Learn from it
Lewdness, immorality

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not disagreeing with the meaning of כומז. He agrees, and only says the proof is clearer from the Hebrew word itself than from the translation.

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
Learn it from the verse itself,
'kumaz' means: here is the place of lewdness.
phrases.notes: The word is read as if it stood for three words.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִגּוּפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a more direct source than רב יוסף's proof from the תרגום.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of כומז as a lewd ornament
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word כומז itself, read as כאן מקום זימה
steps.whatToRemember: All agree that כומז was an immodest ornament. רב יוסף proves it from the תרגום, and רבה proves it from the Hebrew word itself.

steps.title: משה asks the soldiers if they sinned as before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the verse where משה is angry at the army officers. רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה explains that משה suspected they had gone back to their old sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And משה was angry with the officers of the army.' רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: משה said to ישראל, 'Perhaps you have gone back to your first sin?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another verse in the same passage and explains why משה was angry. משה worried the soldiers had sinned with the women of מדין, as they had before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'first sin' is the sin at שטים, when ישראל sinned with the daughters of מואב and מדין. Since the soldiers kept the women of מדין alive, משה feared it was happening again. This opens a back-and-forth between משה and the officers.

keyTerms.meaning: And he was angry
The officers of the army
Perhaps
Your first sin, the sin at שטים

phrases.english: 'And Moses was angry with the officers of the army.'
phrases.notes: במדבר ל״א:י״ד

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Moses said to Israel:
Perhaps you have returned to your original sin?
phrases.notes: This refers to the sin with the daughters of מואב and מדין at שטים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּקְצֹף מֹשֶׁה עַל פְּקוּדֵי הֶחָיִל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the names of the ornaments to the story behind the offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה's anger came from suspecting that the soldiers had sinned with the women of מדין, as at שטים.

steps.title: The soldiers say no one among them sinned
steps.stepSummary: The soldiers answer with the verse 'לא נפקד ממנו איש', meaning not one of them was lacking in proper behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'Not one man of us is missing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The soldiers answer משה's suspicion. They say none of them sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply read, the verse says no soldier died in battle. Here it is read as a moral claim: not one of us is 'missing' from his purity.

keyTerms.meaning: Not missing, not lacking

phrases.english: They said to him: 'Not one man of us is missing.'
phrases.notes: במדבר ל״א:מ״ט. Here it means no one fell into sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's question from Step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did the soldiers return to the sin of שטים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Not one of them sinned.

steps.title: משה asks why they need atonement
steps.stepSummary: משה challenges them: if no one sinned, why are you bringing ornaments for a כפרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If so, why do you need atonement?
steps.whatsHappening: משה points out a contradiction. The soldiers say they did not sin, yet they bring an offering to atone for their souls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says the officers brought the gold 'לכפר על נפשותינו', to atone for our souls. Atonement normally assumes a sin, so their claim of innocence seems to clash with their offering.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Atonement

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: אִם כֵּן כַּפָּרָה לָמָּה?
phrases.english: He said to them: If so, why atonement?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן כַּפָּרָה לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the soldiers' claim of innocence from Step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The soldiers' claim that none of them sinned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there was no sin, there should be no need to bring an offering to atone for their souls.

steps.title: They needed atonement for sinful thoughts
steps.stepSummary: The soldiers explain that they avoided sinful actions but not sinful thoughts. So they immediately brought an offering to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Even if we escaped the hold of sin, we did not escape the hold of sinful thoughts. Immediately: 'And we have brought an offering to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The soldiers answer משה's challenge. Their atonement is for improper thoughts, not for actions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This resolves the contradiction. 'No one sinned' refers to deeds, and the כפרה is for thoughts. That is why they gave the ornaments as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: From the hold of an actual sin
A sinful thought
Immediately
An offering to ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that even sinful thoughts, with no sinful action, call for a כפרה. It also explains why the soldiers' gift of ornaments counted as an offering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם מִידֵי עֲבֵירָה יָצָאנוּ,
phrases.english: They said to him: If we have escaped the hold of transgression,
we have not escaped the hold of sinful thought!
Immediately: 'And we have brought an offering to the Lord.'
phrases.notes: במדבר ל״א:נ׳

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם מִידֵי עֲבֵירָה יָצָאנוּ, מִידֵי הִרְהוּר לֹא יָצָאנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's challenge from Step 35.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כפרה implies that an actual sin was done.
steps.terutzMaskana: They committed no sinful act, but they needed a כפרה for sinful thoughts.
steps.whatToRemember: The soldiers did not sin in action, but they brought the ornaments as an offering to atone for sinful thoughts.

steps.title: A ברייתא asks why that generation needed atonement
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל asks why ישראל in that generation needed a כפרה, and begins to answer. This passage ends mid-sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל: Why did ישראל in that generation need atonement? Because…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that raises the same question about the need for atonement. This step sets up an answer that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks the question that the story just raised. The text breaks off at the start of its answer ('מפני'), so the reason is given in the next section.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
For what reason
They needed

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
For what reason did Israel need
in that generation, atonement?
Because…
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה הוּצְרְכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A ברייתא takes up the same question about the need for atonement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason that generation of ישראל needed a כפרה
